sect1.title: Introduction
sect1.para: The TopMatching class, implemented in Cython, is a specialized selection template within the AnalysisG framework, designed for analyzing top quark matching in Monte Carlo 20 (MC20) events. It inherits from the generic SelectionTemplate class, extending its functionalities to incorporate specific criteria for matching top quarks, particularly with respect to energy limits. This class provides a high-performance interface to an underlying C++ matching object, enabling efficient filtering and analysis based on top quark matching properties.

sect1.title: The TopMatching Class
sect1.para: TopMatching is a cdef class, indicating its implementation as a Cython extension type. It inherits from SelectionTemplate, thereby gaining all the base functionalities for event selection, ROOT file interpretation, and weight management. Its primary role is to encapsulate a C++ matching object, which likely contains the logic for performing top quark matching and applying energy constraints.

listitem.para: __cinit__(self): The Cython "constructor" equivalent, called during object allocation. It initializes a new C++ matching object and assigns its pointer to self.ptr. It then upcasts self.ptr to a matching* and assigns it to self.tt for specialized access.

__dealloc__(self): The Cython "destructor" equivalent, called upon object deallocation. It deallocates the C++ matching object pointed to by self.tt, ensuring proper memory management.

sect1.title: Introduction
sect1.para: The TopMatching class, implemented in Cython, is a specialized selection template within the AnalysisG framework, designed for comprehensive analysis of top quark matching in Monte Carlo 20 (MC20) events. It inherits from the generic SelectionTemplate class, extending its functionalities to extract and organize detailed information about truth-level top quarks, their children, truth-jets, and reconstructed jets, categorized by leptonicity and jet multiplicity. This class facilitates a high-performance extraction and structuring of top matching data for further physics analysis in the MC20 context.

sect1.title: The TopMatching Class
sect1.para: TopMatching is a cdef class, indicating its implementation as a Cython extension type. It inherits from SelectionTemplate, thereby gaining all the base functionalities for event selection, ROOT file interpretation, and weight management. Its primary role is to encapsulate a C++ topmatching object, which likely contains the logic for performing top quark matching and categorizing associated particles and jets.

cdef void transform_dict_keys(self): This method is responsible for converting the C++ data structures within the underlying topmatching object into Python dictionaries and lists, making them accessible as properties of the TopMatching instance.
self.truth_top: Populated from self.tt.truth_top (truth-level top quarks).
self.no_children: Populated from self.tt.no_children (information about top quarks with no children).
self.truth_children: Populated from self.tt.truth_children (truth-level children of top quarks).
self.truth_jets: Populated from self.tt.truth_jets (truth-level jets).
self.n_truth_jets_lep: Populated from self.tt.n_truth_jets_lep (number of leptonic truth-jets).
self.n_truth_jets_had: Populated from self.tt.n_truth_jets_had (number of hadronic truth-jets).
self.jets_truth_leps: Populated from self.tt.jets_truth_leps (jets associated with truth-level leptons).
self.jet_leps: Populated from self.tt.jet_leps (reconstructed jets associated with leptons).
self.n_jets_lep: Populated from self.tt.n_jets_lep (number of leptonic reconstructed jets).
self.n_jets_had: Populated from self.tt.n_jets_had (number of hadronic reconstructed jets).
